newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard seeks higher rate of economic growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard seeks higher rate of economic growth.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday he wanted a higher rate of economic growth.
"I would like to see a higher rate of economic growth," Howard told Melbourne radio 3AW.
"The overall growth figures are still quite strong. We're getting growth, what 3.25 or 3.5 percent, which by world standards is still very good," Howard said.
"I know that in some areas it (economic growth) is not as strong as I would like.
"On the other hand, we have got a set of circumstances that are more, I suppose, attractive for growth and investment than we've had for years."
He said Australia had low inflation, moderate wage growth and falling interest rates.
"What I should do as prime minister is call the thing as it is -- do everything I can to make sure that we keep inflation at a low level, we keep sensible wage demands."
Australia's annual consumer price index inflation was 2.1 percent in the September quarter and wages growth was 3.5 percent annually in the year to August.
The Reserve Bank has cut official interest rates by 1.0 percentage points in two separate reductions in July and earlier this month to 6.5 percent now.
